Absolutely! Here’s a **comprehensive 12-week postpartum return-to-fitness plan** for your client, including strength, core, cardio, and nutrition, with clear week-by-week progression. This plan is tailored for a home/yoga mat setting after an uncomplicated C-section, with OB clearance for light activity at 4 weeks and progressive intensity as she heals.

---

# **12-Week Postpartum Fitness Plan Summary**

---

## **Weeks 1–2: Recovery & Gentle Movement**

**Goals:**  
- Support healing, reconnect with breath and pelvic floor, gentle mobility, light walking.

**Sessions (4–5x/week):**  
- **Breathwork:** Diaphragmatic breathing, gentle Kegels (5–10 reps, 2–3 sets)
- **Mobility:** Cat-cow, neck/shoulder rolls, hip circles, side bends (8–10 reps each)
- **Walking:** 5–10 min, build to 20 min as tolerated, easy pace

**No direct ab work or strength training.**

---

## **Weeks 3–4: Gentle Strength & Mobility**

**Goals:**  
- Maintain mobility, introduce gentle bodyweight strength, continue walking.

**Sessions (4–5x/week):**  
- **Breathwork/Pelvic Floor:** Continue as above
- **Mobility:** Add gentle spinal rotations
- **Strength:**  
  - Wall push-ups: 2 x 8–10  
  - Sit-to-stand: 2 x 8–10  
  - Standing hip abduction: 2 x 10/side  
  - Calf raises: 2 x 10–12  
  - Bird dog arms only: 2 x 8/side
- **Walking:** 10–20 min, easy pace

---

## **Weeks 5–6: Building Endurance**

**Goals:**  
- Increase strength and endurance, prepare for core reintroduction after OB re-clearance.

**Sessions (4–5x/week):**  
- **Breathwork/Pelvic Floor:** Continue
- **Mobility:** Continue
- **Strength:**  
  - Incline push-ups: 2–3 x 8–10  
  - Sit-to-stand: 3 x 10  
  - Glute bridge: 2 x 8–10  
  - Standing hip abduction: 2 x 12/side  
  - Bird dog arms only: 2 x 10/side
- **Walking:** 15–25 min, brisker pace if tolerated

---

## **Weeks 7–8: Gentle Core & Functional Strength**

**Goals:**  
- Begin gentle core engagement, progress bodyweight strength, increase walking duration.

**Sessions (4–5x/week):**  
- **Breathwork/Pelvic Floor:** Continue
- **Core Activation:**  
  - Supine pelvic tilts: 2 x 8–10  
  - Heel slides: 2 x 8–10/side  
  - Dead bug arms only: 2 x 8–10/side
- **Strength:**  
  - Incline push-ups: 3 x 10  
  - Glute bridge: 3 x 10–12  
  - Sit-to-stand: 3 x 12  
  - Standing hip abduction: 2 x 15/side  
  - Bird dog (add gentle leg extension): 2 x 8/side  
  - Supported split squat: 2 x 8/side
- **Walking:** 20–30 min, brisk pace

---

## **Weeks 9–12: Stronger Postpartum (Push Intensity)**

**Goals:**  
- Build full-body strength, challenge core, increase cardio intensity, feel strong by week 12.

**Sessions (4–5x/week):**  
- **Warm-Up:** Cat-cow, hip circles, arm circles, squats, march in place (5 min)
- **Strength Circuits (3–4 rounds):**  
  - **Lower Body & Core:**  
    - Bodyweight squat (with 2-sec pause): 15–20 reps  
    - Reverse lunge (add knee drive): 10–12/side  
    - Single-leg glute bridge: 10–12/side  
    - Side-lying clamshell: 15/side  
    - Dead bug (arms and legs): 12/side  
  - **Upper Body & Core:**  
    - Push-up (incline or floor): 10–15 reps  
    - Triceps dip (off chair): 10–12 reps  
    - Bird dog (full): 12/side  
    - Side plank (knees or full): 20–30 sec/side  
    - Standing Y-T-I raises: 10 each  
  - **Finisher (Optional):**  
    - Squat to calf raise: 15 reps  
    - Mountain climber (slow): 20/side  
    - Bear crawl hold: 20–30 sec  
- **Core Focus (2–3x/week):**  
  - Supine pelvic tilt: 15 reps  
  - Dead bug (arms and legs): 12/side  
  - Side plank: 20–30 sec/side  
  - Modified plank (on knees or full): 20–30 sec  
  - Heel tap: 12/side  
- **Cardio:**  
  - Brisk walk: 30–40 min, or  
  - Walking intervals: 3 min brisk, 1 min easy x 6–8 rounds  
  - Mat-based low-impact cardio circuit (march, step touch, squat to reach, knee lifts): 3–4 rounds, 1 min each  
- **Mobility/Active Recovery:** 1–2x/week

---

## **Cardio Progression**

| Weeks | Cardio Focus         | Frequency | Duration      | Intensity         |
|-------|----------------------|-----------|---------------|-------------------|
| 1–4   | Gentle walking       | 4–5x/week | 5–20 min      | Easy              |
| 5–8   | Brisk walking/intervals | 4–5x/week | 20–30 min      | Moderate          |
| 9–12  | Intervals & mat cardio | 4–5x/week | 25–40 min      | Moderate–hard     |

---

## **Core/Abs Work Timeline**

- **Weeks 1–6:** No direct ab work; focus on breath, pelvic floor, gentle core engagement.
- **Weeks 7–12:** Gentle core activation (pelvic tilts, heel slides, dead bug, bird dog, side plank).
- **After 12 weeks:** If symptom-free and cleared, may introduce traditional abs (plank, crunch, etc.)—progress slowly.

---

## **Nutrition Plan for Breastfeeding**

- **Calories:** 2,200–2,700 kcal/day (individualized)
- **Macros:**  
  - Protein: 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day  
  - Carbs: 45–55%  
  - Fats: 25–35% (focus on healthy fats)
- **Hydration:** 3–4 liters/day
- **Micronutrients:**  
  - Calcium, iron, vitamin D, omega-3s (DHA)
  - Continue prenatal vitamins
- **Sample Day:**  
  - Oatmeal with chia, berries, nut butter  
  - Greek yogurt, fruit, nuts  
  - Whole grain wrap with protein, veggies, avocado  
  - Apple with peanut butter  
  - Salmon/tofu, quinoa, veggies  
  - Cottage cheese, fruit
- **Tips:**  
  - Eat 3 meals + 2–3 snacks  
  - Batch cook, keep easy snacks handy  
  - Include galactagogues (oats, flaxseed, leafy greens)  
  - Limit caffeine (<300 mg/day), alcohol (wait 2–3 hrs before feeding if consumed)

---

## **HIIT Timeline**

- **Not before 12 weeks postpartum.**
- **12–16+ weeks:** If symptom-free and cleared, start with low-impact HIIT (fast march, step touch, squats, etc.).
- **16–24+ weeks:** Add higher-impact HIIT only if pelvic floor/core are strong and symptom-free.

---

## **Key Safety & Progression Notes**

- **Monitor for:** Pain, bleeding, pelvic heaviness, incontinence, doming/coning—regress if any occur.
- **Progression:** Increase reps, sets, rounds, or tempo as tolerated.
- **Form:** Prioritize quality over quantity.
- **Rest:** Take extra rest as needed, especially with sleep deprivation.
- **Refer:** To pelvic health physio if any core/pelvic floor symptoms persist.

---

**By week 12, she’ll have rebuilt foundational strength, core stability, and cardiovascular fitness, and will be ready for more advanced training or a return to her favorite activities.**
